extraction.name: COMMONSENSE QA
extraction.description: A question answering challenge dataset targeting commonsense knowledge consisting of 12,247 multiple-choice questions. Questions are authored by crowd-workers based on subgraphs extracted from ConceptNet, requiring background knowledge to discriminate between semantically similar target concepts.
extraction.creator: Alon Talmor, Jonathan Herzig, Nicholas Lourie, Jonathan Berant
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Subgraphs containing one source concept and three target concepts with the same relation were extracted from ConceptNet. Amazon Mechanical Turk crowd-workers authored three natural language questions per subgraph and added two distractors per question. A disjoint group of workers verified the questions, and context was gathered by retrieving web search snippets using Google search for each question and candidate answer.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, User-generated content data, Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: ConceptNet knowledge graph and web search result snippets from Google search.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: ConceptNet triplets were filtered to 22 relations by removing general relations or those already well-explored in NLP, triplets where concepts have more than four words or are not in English, and triplets where the edit distance between concepts was too low. For question verification, questions were filtered out if not verified by at least one worker who answered correctly, removing 15% of the questions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Crowd-workers on Amazon Mechanical Turk authored three questions per subgraph that discriminated between target concepts and avoided words with strong relation to the answer. Workers also selected one additional distractor from ConceptNet and manually authored another distractor. A disjoint group of AMT workers verified questions by choosing the correct answer or marking them unanswerable.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Each question was verified by 2 workers, and only questions verified by at least one worker who answered correctly were retained. For human baseline evaluation, majority voting across 5 workers was used on a sample of 100 questions.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 122 formulators contributed to question generation, with 10 workers formulating more than 85% of the questions. Only annotators whose questions had at least a 75% pass rate in verification were accepted.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The paper notes reporting bias on the web where trivial background knowledge is seldom explicitly reported. It also observes potential annotator distribution bias, noting that 10 workers formulated more than 85% of the questions, as well as discussing annotation artifacts commonly found in crowdsourced commonsense datasets.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation for commonsense question answering and reading comprehension models.
